notes: Source is Luminex's own PDF datasheet "Technical specifications GigaCore 10i v1.0.2" (product page: https://www.luminex.be/products/gigacore/gigacore-10i/). There is no product literally named "GigaCore 10 PoE" in Luminex's current lineup — the 10-port AV switch family branches into GigaCore 10i (compact ½-19" installation unit, this entry), GigaCore 10t (touring unit with etherCON ports + PowerCON power, also offered with an optional PoE++ variant), and GigaCore 10t-IP (weatherproof). PoE is an ordering option on the base chassis, not a separate model line: standard SKU is "GigaCore 10i-8x1G-2x10G(SFP+)" (LU 01 00089-10G) and the PoE++ SKU used here is "GigaCore 10i-8x1G-2x10G(SFP+)-PoE++" (LU 01 00089-10G-POE). If the touring "10t" chassis was intended instead, its physical ports differ (8x etherCON copper + 2x ruggedized fiber, 1x PowerCON True1 power inlet). Front-panel port numbering (1–8 for copper, 9–10 for the SFP+ cages) is read off the datasheet's front-panel photo; exact silkscreen labels for the two SFP+ slots were not fully legible in text extraction. The datasheet's PoE table oddly lists "PoE Ports ... On ports 1-24," which is inconsistent with this 8-copper-port unit and appears to be a copy/paste artifact from a larger-port GigaCore model's spec sheet — the applications-page text and PoE budget figures (90W/port, 180W total across 8 ports) are used instead as the reliable figures. Half-19" chassis (220 x 296.4 x 43.2 mm) is listed as rackUnits: 1 based on its ~1U height, though it occupies only half the rack width (mounts via VESA 100x100 points or side-by-side with a second half-width GigaCore unit to fill a full 19" 1U rack space). Ethernet grade (eth-1g) was applied only to the 8 fixed RJ45 copper ports; grade was omitted on the 2 SFP+ cages per the schema's fiber/pluggable-port exclusion, even though the datasheet states they run up to 10Gbps/1Gbps.
